concepts.description: Introduces the role of information and communication technology in daily life, education, business, and communication.

questions.questionText: What does ICT stand for?
questions.explanation: ICT is the short form for Information and Communication Technology.

questions.questionText: Which activity is an example of using ICT in education?
questions.explanation: Learning management systems are ICT tools used to share lessons and assignments.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a major benefit of ICT?
questions.explanation: ICT improves speed when storing, searching, and sharing information.

questions.questionText: A smartphone is considered an ICT device mainly because it can:
questions.explanation: ICT devices help users create, process, store, and share information.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the role of ICT in modern society?
options: It supports communication, automation, and data handling
It removes the need for networks
It is used only in offices
questions.correctAnswer: It supports communication, automation, and data handling
questions.explanation: ICT has a broad role across communication, learning, work, and information management.

concepts.description: Covers the physical parts of a computer system such as input, output, storage, and processing devices.

questions.questionText: Which hardware component is known as the brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and controls major operations.

questions.questionText: Which device is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends data and commands into the computer.

questions.questionText: Which of these is used for long-term data storage?
questions.explanation: An SSD stores data permanently even when power is off.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of RAM?
options: Temporarily store data currently in use
questions.correctAnswer: Temporarily store data currently in use
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory used while programs are running.

questions.questionText: A scanner is classified as which type of hardware?
questions.explanation: A scanner captures information and sends it into the computer.

concepts.description: Explains software categories, including system software and application software, and their purposes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is software?
questions.explanation: Software consists of programs and instructions, unlike physical hardware parts.

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between hardware and software?
options: Hardware is physical, software is intangible
Hardware is faster, software is slower
Hardware is free, software is paid
questions.correctAnswer: Hardware is physical, software is intangible
questions.explanation: Hardware can be touched, while software is a set of programs and instructions.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of system software?
questions.explanation: System software manages hardware and provides a base for applications.

questions.questionText: A word processor is best classified as:
questions.explanation: Application software helps users perform specific tasks such as typing documents.

questions.questionText: Why are utility programs grouped under system software?
options: They help manage and maintain the computer
questions.correctAnswer: They help manage and maintain the computer
questions.explanation: Utilities support tasks like cleaning, backup, antivirus, and file management.

concepts.description: Focuses on the purpose of an operating system and basic operating system functions such as file and device management.

questions.questionText: What is the main role of an operating system?
questions.explanation: The OS coordinates hardware, files, memory, and application execution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an operating system, while the others are applications or content.

questions.questionText: Which task is handled by an operating system?
questions.explanation: File management is one of the standard functions of an operating system.

questions.questionText: Why is device management important in an operating system?
options: It lets the OS control peripherals correctly
questions.correctAnswer: It lets the OS control peripherals correctly
questions.explanation: The OS manages communication between the computer and connected devices.

questions.questionText: A graphical user interface helps users by:
options: Providing icons and windows for interaction
questions.correctAnswer: Providing icons and windows for interaction
questions.explanation: A GUI makes interaction easier through visual elements like icons, menus, and windows.

concepts.description: Introduces how computers represent text, numbers, images, and sound using bits and bytes.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest unit of data in computing?
questions.explanation: A bit stores one binary value, either 0 or 1.

questions.questionText: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.explanation: A byte is made up of 8 bits.

questions.questionText: Computers represent data internally using:
questions.explanation: Computer circuits naturally work with two states, so data is stored in binary form.

questions.questionText: Which statement about text encoding is correct?
options: Characters are mapped to numeric codes
Every letter is stored as an image
Text can only be stored in decimal
questions.correctAnswer: Characters are mapped to numeric codes
questions.explanation: Encoding standards such as ASCII and Unicode represent characters using numbers.

questions.questionText: Why are images and sounds also converted into binary?
options: Because computers process all digital data as binary
Because binary is a type of cable
questions.correctAnswer: Because computers process all digital data as binary
questions.explanation: Different media types are encoded into binary so computers can store and process them.

concepts.description: Explains decimal, binary, octal, and hexadecimal number systems and basic conversions.

questions.questionText: What is the base of the binary number system?
questions.explanation: Binary uses only two symbols, 0 and 1, so its base is 2.

questions.questionText: Which binary number equals decimal 5?
questions.explanation: Binary 101 equals 1x4 + 0x2 + 1x1 = 5.

questions.questionText: Which number system commonly uses digits 0-9 and letters A-F?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses sixteen symbols: 0-9 and A-F.

questions.questionText: What is decimal 10 in binary?
questions.explanation: Decimal 10 equals 8 + 2, which is binary 1010.

questions.questionText: Why is hexadecimal useful in computing?
options: It gives a shorter representation of binary values
It is only used for typing letters
questions.correctAnswer: It gives a shorter representation of binary values
questions.explanation: One hexadecimal digit can represent four binary bits, which makes values easier to read.

concepts.description: Introduces basic digital logic gates and how truth tables describe their behavior.

questions.questionText: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1?
questions.explanation: The AND gate is true only when all inputs are true.

questions.questionText: What does a NOT gate do?
questions.explanation: A NOT gate changes 1 to 0 and 0 to 1.

questions.questionText: If the inputs of an OR gate are 0 and 1, the output is:
questions.explanation: An OR gate gives 1 when at least one input is 1.

questions.questionText: A truth table is used to show:
options: All input and output combinations of a logic circuit
questions.correctAnswer: All input and output combinations of a logic circuit
questions.explanation: Truth tables summarize how outputs change for every possible input combination.

questions.questionText: Which pair of gates is most directly linked to binary decision making?
questions.explanation: AND and OR gates are core components used to build digital decision logic.

concepts.description: Explains how computers connect to share data and resources using wired and wireless networks.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a computer network?
questions.explanation: Networks allow devices to communicate and share files, printers, and Internet access.

questions.questionText: A network limited to a school lab is usually a:
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network covers a small geographical area like a room, office, or school.

questions.questionText: Which device forwards data between different networks?
questions.explanation: Routers direct data packets between networks.

questions.questionText: Which is an advantage of networking computers in an office?
questions.explanation: Networks reduce duplication by enabling shared access to devices and documents.

questions.questionText: Wireless networking mainly differs from wired networking because it uses:
questions.explanation: Wireless networks transmit data through radio waves instead of physical cables.

concepts.description: Covers Internet services, web browsing, search, and the proper use of email communication.

questions.questionText: Which software is mainly used to browse websites?
questions.explanation: A browser is the application used to open and navigate websites.

questions.questionText: What does email allow users to do?
questions.explanation: Email is a communication service for sending digital messages and attachments.

questions.questionText: Which part of an email address appears after the @ symbol?
questions.explanation: The domain identifies the email service or organization hosting the address.

questions.questionText: Why is the subject line important in an email?
options: It summarizes the purpose of the message
questions.correctAnswer: It summarizes the purpose of the message
questions.explanation: A clear subject helps the receiver understand the message quickly.

questions.questionText: Which action is a good Internet search practice?
options: Typing a full paragraph every time
questions.explanation: Specific keywords improve search accuracy and help users find better results.

concepts.description: Introduces safe digital behavior, common cyber threats, and methods to protect devices and information.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best example of a strong password?
questions.explanation: Strong passwords usually mix letters, numbers, and symbols and avoid common words.

questions.questionText: What is phishing?
options: A trick to steal personal information
questions.correctAnswer: A trick to steal personal information
questions.explanation: Phishing attacks pretend to be trustworthy to obtain passwords or other private data.

questions.questionText: Why should software updates be installed regularly?
questions.explanation: Updates often patch weaknesses attackers could exploit.

questions.questionText: Which behavior is safest when receiving an unexpected email attachment?
options: Verify the sender before opening it
questions.correctAnswer: Verify the sender before opening it
questions.explanation: Checking the sender reduces the risk of opening malicious files.

questions.questionText: Why is backing up important for cyber security?
options: It helps recover data after loss or attack
It removes the need for storage
questions.correctAnswer: It helps recover data after loss or attack
questions.explanation: Backups provide a safe copy of data if the original is deleted, damaged, or encrypted by malware.

concepts.description: Teaches document creation, editing, formatting, and common features of word processing software.

questions.questionText: Which application is mainly used to create letters and reports?
questions.explanation: Word processors are designed for preparing and formatting text documents.

questions.questionText: What does spell check help a user do?
questions.explanation: Spell check highlights misspelled words and often suggests corrections.

questions.questionText: Changing font size and style is part of:
questions.explanation: Formatting changes the visual appearance of text and layout.

questions.questionText: Why are headers and footers useful in a document?
options: They add repeated information like titles or page numbers
questions.correctAnswer: They add repeated information like titles or page numbers
questions.explanation: Headers and footers help keep repeated document information consistent.

questions.questionText: Which feature is best for replacing every occurrence of one word with another?
questions.explanation: Find and Replace updates repeated text efficiently across a document.

concepts.description: Introduces spreadsheet structure, formulas, functions, and data organization.

questions.questionText: A spreadsheet is mainly organized into:
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets store data in a grid of rows and columns.

questions.questionText: What symbol usually starts a formula in a spreadsheet?
questions.explanation: Formulas usually begin with the equals sign so the application evaluates them.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to add a range of numbers?
questions.explanation: SUM is the standard function for totaling numeric values.

questions.questionText: What is cell B3?
options: The cell at column B and row 3
questions.correctAnswer: The cell at column B and row 3
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet cells are named by column letter followed by row number.

questions.questionText: Why are spreadsheets useful for marks analysis?
options: They can calculate and summarize data quickly
They are only for typing essays
questions.correctAnswer: They can calculate and summarize data quickly
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets make calculations, sorting, filtering, and charting efficient.

concepts.description: Introduces records, fields, tables, and the purpose of databases in organizing large sets of related data.

questions.questionText: What is a database mainly used for?
questions.explanation: Databases are built to store, search, and manage structured data efficiently.

questions.questionText: In a student table, 'Student Name' is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A field represents a single attribute or data item in a table.

questions.questionText: A single row in a database table is called a:
questions.explanation: A record stores all the fields for one item or person.

questions.questionText: Why is a primary key useful in a database?
options: It is used only for email
questions.explanation: A primary key prevents ambiguity by giving each record a unique identifier.

questions.questionText: What does a query do in a database?
options: Searches or filters data based on conditions
questions.correctAnswer: Searches or filters data based on conditions
questions.explanation: Queries help users retrieve the exact records they need from a database.

concepts.description: Introduces variables, input, output, sequence, selection, and repetition in simple programming logic.

questions.questionText: What is a variable in programming?
options: A named storage location for data
questions.correctAnswer: A named storage location for data
questions.explanation: Variables store values that a program can use or change.

questions.questionText: Which programming structure means steps happen one after another?
questions.explanation: Sequence executes instructions in order from top to bottom.

questions.questionText: An IF statement is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: IF statements allow programs to choose actions based on conditions.

questions.questionText: What is repetition in programming?
options: Running a set of instructions multiple times
questions.correctAnswer: Running a set of instructions multiple times
questions.explanation: Loops repeat instructions while a condition is met or for a set count.

questions.questionText: Why is input important in many programs?
questions.explanation: Programs often need data from the user, file, or device before producing useful output.

concepts.description: Covers step-by-step problem solving, algorithms, and flowchart symbols used to represent logic clearly.

questions.questionText: What is an algorithm?
options: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
questions.correctAnswer: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is an ordered set of instructions for completing a task or solving a problem.

questions.questionText: Which flowchart symbol is commonly used for a decision?
questions.explanation: The diamond shape usually represents a yes/no or true/false decision point.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is commonly used for a process step?
questions.explanation: A rectangle is the standard flowchart symbol for a processing action.

questions.questionText: Why are flowcharts useful before writing code?
questions.explanation: Flowcharts make the order of steps and decisions easier to review before coding.

questions.questionText: An algorithm should ideally be:
questions.explanation: Good algorithms have clear steps, a logical order, and an ending point.
